pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert — service: embed-inference-prod, trigger: request_error_rate > 5% for 2m. Priority: P2. Escalation: notify oncall (SRE) and eng-runtime. Link: https://pd.example/redwood/INC123456
incident-bot: Automated check: canary rollout id=rollout_2026_03_14_09, stage=staged, batch=3/10. Error pattern: 502s at ingress, p99 lat 2.3s -> 4.8s.
Maya: ack @pagerduty-bot — I'm oncall. Pulling logs now.
Dmitri: on it too, checking canary infra metrics and recent kernel warnings.
Lina: adding context: Dedicated customers in eu-west-1 reporting increased 5xxs. No alerts from dedicated-only metric prior to rollout.
Joel: quick question — did the new quant kernel land in this rollout? I remember an opt-in in batch 2.
Maya: yes batch 2 included kernel v2.1-quant. batch 3 had traffic shift to that variant.
Sam: seeing similar traces — KV cache misses spike right before 502. attaching trace id: trace-0a7c
Maya: Repro attempt: curl -v -H 'x-redwood-tenant: ded-123' https://embed.prod.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
Maya: returns 502 and logs: 
```
E 03/14 09:04:17 upstream response: read ECONNRESET from worker-12
W 03/14 09:04:17 kv-cache: miss for session 0x4f22
E 03/14 09:04:18 quant-kernel: oom-ish fallback; aborting token loop
```
Dmitri: looks like worker OOM / segfault-ish behavior with the new kernel under a specific token pattern. Might be memory footprint increase in batch 3.
incident-bot: Escalation schedule: if not resolved in 5m, escalate to SRE lead.
Maya: I'm going to pause the rollout and divert traffic back to stable model 2026-03-13-rt. Executing: `redwoodctl rollout pause rollout_2026_03_14_09`
Joel: please also run `redwoodctl route update --policy=stable --target=model:2026-03-13-rt --scope=batch=3` so live traffic stops hitting the canary.
Maya: ran both commands — pause returned OK. Route update applied. Confirming traffic drop to batch 3.
Lina: Customer impact: Dedicated tenants ded-123 and ded-777 observed elevated error rates for ~3 minutes; CS notified via incident bridge.
Sam: Dumped worker logs from worker-12, posted link to S3 (https://s3.example/redwood/errdump/trace-0a7c.log). There's a soft OOM pattern followed by abrupt worker exit.
Dmitri: can we restart affected kube nodes? Might be a transient memory leak. But prefer rollback first to avoid more impacted sessions.
Maya: decision: rollback kernel patch from batch 2/3 and resume with stable runtime. Plan: rollback batch 3 -> batch 2 -> validate for 2 minutes, then continue staged rollout after manual signoff.
Joel: I'll open a PR to pin the runtime config and block the kernel opt-in until we finish stress tests.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident status changed to acknowledged by Maya. Unacknowledged escalation suppressed.
pagerduty-bot: Note: PagerDuty note — escalation timer paused.
Lina: CS update draft for customers: "We observed elevated error rates during a partial rollout affecting some Dedicated tenants in eu-west-1. We have paused the rollout and reverted traffic to the last-stable model. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause once we have more data." Approve?
Maya: approve. Send now.
Sam: after rollback, p99 dropped back to ~1.1s and 502s stopped. Monitoring for 10m.
Dmitri: scheduling postmortem with kernel team and runtime SRE. Tentative RCA track: quant-kernel memory growth under kv-cache churn.
Maya: handing off to post-incident ops: Lina (CS) will own customer comms, Joel will follow release gating, Dmitri + Sam will lead RCA, Maya will run remediation follow-through.
Maya: closing PD incident after 20m stable. Will update thread with postmortem link when ready. :checkered_flag:
incident-bot: Incident resolved. Duration 00:23:33. Follow-up tasks assigned: #RCA-489, #RolloutPolicy-22.
Joel: noted action: add automated pre-rollout smoke that includes kv-cache stress and memory accounting.
Lina: sent customer notes and opened support tickets for affected tenants.
Sam: uploading core dump analysis to /internal/incidents/3380012345/coredump_analysis.md
Maya: thanks everyone. Great quick coordination.
